title: Why Do You Think the Ocean Is Salty?
summary: Rain slowly washes tiny amounts of minerals out of rocks and rivers carry them to the sea. Water evaporates, but the salt stays behind.

beats.text: Why is the sea salty, when rivers are not? Is it fish, rocks, or volcanoes? Pause and guess!
Rivers taste fresh. Yet every river ends in the sea.
Time's up. Where does the salt come from?
beats.reveal: Rocks! Rain wears tiny bits of minerals out of rock, and rivers carry them to the sea.

visual.question: Where does most sea salt come from?

beats.text: The sun lifts pure water into clouds. The salt can't float away, so it stays behind.
Over millions of years, the sea keeps getting a little saltier.
Bonus fact: in the Dead Sea, the water is so salty you float without trying.

visual.text: In the very salty Dead Sea, you float easily, because salty water is denser.
